findings.headline: High stress on lap 15 did not degrade pace – no pit‑stop adjustment required
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 79.2 on lap 15 while the driver was on a 15‑lap old MEDIUM tyre on a drying surface (track 24.6 °C, dry) and still holding P1. Pace delta was -0.10 s/lap (strategy rule HOLD) and lap time stayed at the median, indicating the driver can sustain high stress without losing pace; no pit‑stop change is needed.
evidence: pace delta -0.10 on lap 15 (derived from strategy rule)

findings.headline: Wet track caused >1.5 s slowdown on lap 18 – consider earlier intermediate stop
findings.detail: From lap 18 onward the medium tyre showed a modelled degradation of +0.181 s/lap, and pace delta jumped +1.572 s on lap 18 as the track became wet (track 24.3 °C, wet). The driver’s stress reading was not recorded, but the sudden slowdown aligns with tyre‑performance loss on a wet surface; an earlier switch to intermediates could have limited the 1.6 s loss.

findings.headline: Old medium tyres on wet track caused >5 s loss on lap 20 – fresh intermediates improved stability
findings.detail: During laps 20‑22 the medium tyre on a fully wet surface (track 22.5‑22.1 °C) produced a +5.169 s pace delta on lap 20, then recovered to -0.624 s on lap 22 after the driver received a BLUE flag and cleared traffic. The large variance suggests the driver was struggling with grip on old mediums; the subsequent pit on lap 28 to fresh intermediates stabilised pace (lap 31 still +0.332 s, lap 32 +1.183 s).

findings.headline: Post‑race stress high on lap 33; pace still acceptable but watch fatigue on intermediates
findings.detail: Stress reading of 77.9 on lap 33 comes from post‑race radio, not an in‑lap measurement, yet the model shows a pace delta of +0.332 s (lap 31) and +1.183 s (lap 32) on fresh intermediates, indicating the driver was already feeling tired while still managing moderate pace; monitor for fatigue in longer wet stints.

findings.headline: Blue‑flag periods yielded no pace improvement – consider aggressive line when traffic clears
findings.detail: Blue flags from laps 21‑27 coincided with flat pace deltas (0.0 s) on the medium tyre despite worsening wet conditions, suggesting the driver maintained position without overtaking effort; however, the lack of pace gain indicates missed opportunity to push when traffic cleared.
